trial_court: IV Additional District Judge-cum- Family Court, Kurnool (F.C.O.P.No.20 of 2016)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: husband, filed petition under Order VI Rule 17 C.P.C for amendment of pleadings
parties.respondent_defendant: wife, respondent in the divorce petition

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife has converted to another religion; petitioner seeks amendment of pleadings to add ground of change of religion in divorce petition; trial court dismissed the petition saying conversion must be subsequent to marriage

legal_principles.principle: Conversion to another religion must be subsequent to the marriage.
legal_principles.held: Section 13(1)(ii) of the Act reveals that the party 'ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion' whether before or after commencement of the Act.

legal_principles.principle: Evidence is required to prove conversion to another religion.
legal_principles.held: Whether the petitioner has converted into Christian; or Whether the respondent has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion are questions of fact, which can be decided only after adducing evidence by both the parties and also on production of relevant documents if there are any.

legal_principles.principle: The court must not make findings without sufficient evidence.
legal_principles.held: The said findings of trial Court are also not correct without there being sufficient evidence with regard to conversion into Christianity.

outcome.final_order: Petition under Order VI Rule 17 C.P.C for amendment of pleadings is allowed.
